tldr: A single canonical population transport-map query has squared minimax risk \(n^{-4/7}\) when the rough propensity is unknown and \(n^{-10/11}\) when the exact propensity is supplied on the same factual records. Both rates are attained by total finite estimators over the unchanged class, and both converses apply to all randomized Borel rules. The information penalty is of order \(n^{26/77}\). The upper proof combines certified finite gradient-map pilots, source smoothing, moving-pole elliptic response and shell-specific original-record corrections. Uniform pilot logarithms are strictly subleading and do not enter either minimax rate.
